rsit-01: Pons, Harris & de Rosnay: hidden and mixed emotions (Test of Emotion Comprehension components)
rsit-02: Gross process model of emotion regulation: noticing body cues before responding
rsit-03: Compas control-based coping: secondary-control coping (reappraisal, acceptance) vs disengagement
rsit-04: Inhibitory control and delay of gratification (Diamond 2013 executive functions); honesty after a slip
rsit-05: Dodge social information processing: ambiguous provocation and hostile attribution bias
rsit-06: Pons TEC desire-based emotion; Selman social-informational perspective taking (about ages 5-9)
rsit-07: Turiel social domain theory: a welfare (moral) concern outranks a classroom convention
rsit-08: WHO life skills: decision making; Turiel moral domain (another child's loss)
rsit-09: Ethic of Community in Indian children's moral reasoning (Pandya and colleagues); duty to younger siblings
rsit-10: Pons TEC external causes of emotion; Compas engagement vs disengagement coping
rsit-12: Dodge hostile attribution bias, applied to an ambiguous online cue
rsit-13: Pons TEC hidden emotions: the feeling shown differs from the feeling inside
rsit-14: WHO life skills: coping with stress and empathy; help-seeking through a trusted adult
rsit-15: WHO life skills: empathy; inclusion of a child with a disability (upstander response)
rsit-16: Cognitive reappraisal development in adolescence (Willner et al. 2022 systematic review)
rsit-17: Pons TEC mixed emotions (two feelings about one event)
rsit-18: WHO life skills: effective communication (assertive, not aggressive)
rsit-19: Online safety (VS-DIGI in the design set): personal information and telling a trusted adult
rsit-20: Turiel moral domain: fairness to others vs group convenience
rsit-21: Ethic of Community and duty reasoning in Indian adolescents (Pandya and colleagues); a dilemma with more than one okay answer
rsit-22: Compas primary-control coping (problem solving) vs disengagement; WHO coping with stress
ysit-01: Desire-based emotion (Pons, Harris & de Rosnay, Test of Emotion Comprehension): the same event makes one child happy and another sad because they wanted different things; understood from about age 5.
ysit-02: Ambiguous provocation and hostile attribution (Dodge, social information processing): checking before assuming someone meant harm.
ysit-03: Gross process model of emotion regulation: noticing the body's signals of anger before acting on them.
ysit-04: Inhibitory control and delay of gratification (Diamond 2013): waiting for something tempting, helped by a smart way to wait.
ysit-05: WHO life skills (decision making): owning up to a mistake nobody saw, and helping put it right.
ysit-06: Inclusion of a child who is different (WHO life skills: empathy); upstander responses at an age-appropriate level.
ysit-07: WHO life skills (coping with stress): help-seeking through a trusted grown-up; staying put when lost.
ysit-08: Fairness and turn-taking in early and middle childhood: finding a fair way that works for both.
ysit-09: Turiel social domain theory: young children can see that someone being hurt matters more than a 'be quiet' rule.
ysit-10: Hidden emotion (Pons, Harris & de Rosnay, Test of Emotion Comprehension): noticing a clue that someone feels different inside from what they show.
ysit-11: Online safety: never sharing personal details with someone unknown, and telling a trusted grown-up.
ysit-12: WHO life skills (effective communication): saying clearly and calmly what you need, instead of hitting out or staying silent.
ypz-01: Early number: adding within 10 with a story.
ypz-02: Early number: taking away within 10 with a story.
ypz-03: Early reasoning: continuing a repeating pattern.
